correctness.rationale: For the specified labelled Heawood graph the non-incidence maps α and β are antitone Galois adjoints: Y⊆α(X) iff X⊆β(Y). The triple-composition identities give F³=F, not merely an eventual period-two bound. F² applies the idempotent closure separately to each shore; its image is the complete recurrent state set. Point sets of sizes 0, 1, and 2 close to themselves: for any outside point some line through it avoids the set. For three points, inclusion–exclusion on their three incident-line stars gives six hit lines when noncollinear, seven when collinear. Thus a noncollinear triple closes to the complement of its unique avoiding line; every such complement has its four three-subsets and itself in its fiber. All other sets of size at least three close to the full set. This gives 37 closed symbols with the stated five fiber types and an all-points fiber of size 128−(1+7+21+35)=64. Anti-incidence interchanges empty/full, singleton/line-complement and pair/pair types. On the closed product, the update swaps the two dual labels; the 37 diagonal states are fixed and the 666 unordered unequal pairs are primitive two-cycle orbits. Basin sizes are one product of the two closure-fiber sizes for a diagonal, or the sum of the two ordered products for an unordered pair. This gives the stated 11 rows, fixed mass 219, period-two mass 16165, and the four entry counts; the empty/full symbol pair alone gives 4097. Independently reproduced the full census from Fano lines given by binary projective triples and by traversing each trajectory until its first repeated state, without assuming any bound on entry or period. It reproduced every row, the four entry counts and the empty/full orbit size. Replay: python3 -B /workspace/reproductions/check.py 3; output /workspace/reproductions/3.log. The frozen C++ and Python files and census were inspected as evidence, not run.
residual_risks: Result concerns the labelled graph and synchronous open-neighborhood NOR only. The finite census does not certify any broader dynamical variant.

evidence: Aracena–Richard–Salinas give fix(G^−)=mis(G) (eq. 2) and the loopless symmetric negative AND–NOT fixed-point correspondence (2014 Proposition 1). This is the same map on fixed configurations.

The closed antitone pairs are maximal nonincidence rectangles, and their fibers classify preimages under the two shore closures. The general symmetric NOR map itself is a self-adjoint nonincidence operator on vertex subsets, so F³=F does not require the Fano structure.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Existence or enumeration of maximal independent sets is not a census of preimages and basins. The same-object fixed-point reformulation is credited; the Fano-specific fiber sizes are needed for the claimed basin table.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical smallest nontrivial projective-plane incidence graph, so the host is motivated independently of the census. A complete, reproducible 703-orbit benchmark distinguishes attraction from mere orbit counts; in particular it separates 21 isolated equilibria from the empty/full orbit with 4097 initial states. The fiber geometry explains those values and gives a useful comparison point for other incidence networks or rules, without claiming any downstream theorem.
residual_risks: Value is the precise invariant of this graph and rule; not a new general algorithm or a claim about all Boolean network dynamics.
